common_name: Big Pink Autumn Sage (Large-Flowered Pink Salvia greggii, Saltillo Selection)

planting.note: Plant container plants in spring in well-drained, average to lean soil in full sun for the heaviest bloom.

directions: Plant in well-drained, average to lean soil in full sun. Big Pink was collected near Saltillo, Mexico, and stands out among Salvia greggii selections for its unusually large, violet-pink flowers set off by contrasting dark maroon calyces on a rigidly upright, shiny-leaved shrub. It flowers heavily from late spring into summer and again from late summer through fall, drawing hummingbirds and bees throughout its long bloom season. Spent flower stalks persist rather than dropping cleanly, so shear the shrub back by half to two-thirds in late winter to remove them and renew dense, floriferous growth. Highly drought-tolerant once established and rarely browsed by deer.

common_name: Dark Dancer Autumn Sage (Raspberry-Red Salvia greggii, Nevin Smith Selection)

planting.note: Plant container plants in spring in well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade; needs little supplemental water once rooted in.

directions: Plant in well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade with little supplemental water once established. Dark Dancer arose as a garden seedling discovered near Nevin Smith's Aptos, California nursery and forms a wide, glossy-leaved clump of narrow, lightly fragrant foliage topped with showy raspberry-red to deep reddish-purple flowers and near-black calyces. Bloom is heaviest in spring and fall with a lighter, sporadic show through the muggy heart of summer, and hummingbirds visit constantly. Its wide, mounding habit makes it a useful colorful groundcover on slopes and banks. Cut back hard in late winter to keep the clump tidy and encourage the next flush of growth.

common_name: Diane Autumn Sage (Compact Bicolor Reddish-Purple Salvia greggii)

planting.note: Plant container plants in spring in well-drained soil in full sun; tolerates poor, rocky soil once rooted in.

directions: Plant in well-drained, average soil in full sun. Diane is a compact, dwarf Salvia greggii selection that stays under two feet tall while spreading into a dense, deer-resistant clump, making it useful as a dry-garden groundcover, border edger, or patio container plant. Its small flowers shift between deep reddish-purple and vivid pink depending on light and temperature, giving the shrub an unusually variable bicolor effect through its peak spring and fall bloom flushes. Hummingbirds and beneficial insects visit steadily whenever it is in flower. Cut back by about half in late winter to remove old wood and keep the compact habit dense and floriferous.
